short: Sweden's first modern constitution, formalizing the central state administration.
full:
Adopted by the Riksdag on 29 July 1634, the Instrument of Government (Regeringsform) was primarily drafted by Axel Oxenstierna. It established a formalized, centralized administrative structure for the Swedish realm, organizing the government into five permanent colleges, each headed by a high officer of state.

The document transformed Sweden from a state dependent on the monarch's personal rule into a modern, bureaucratic administration capable of functioning independently of the sovereign. It proved crucial in ensuring governmental stability during Queen Christina's minority and the prolonged absences of Swedish kings engaged in foreign wars.
